The last three weeks of class are dedicated to in-class workshops in which students work through the research process: identifying a topic, formulating and narrowing a research question, finding relevant sources, reading those sources strategically, outlining the paper, and drafting it. 

These workshops help limit AI use in several ways. First, students have enough time to work through, and even enjoy, the research process; because they are not rushed, they are less tempted to turn to AI. Second, working in class keeps students accountable throughout the learning process. Finally, students know their professor values the process over the final product, so they are more invested in engaging with that process than in producing a flawless paper.
